body.statement: Using \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{enum}}\), can one construct an output-polynomial or polynomial-delay algorithm that emits each distinct rational total-effect functional \(g_E\), for \(E\in\mathcal R(C)\), exactly once and returns a certificate partitioning all states by functional equality, while preserving the shortest legal-reversal certificates from \(C\)? The construction must derive path independence of transported partitions and may not assume that numerically coincident evaluations identify equal rational functionals.
body.justification: State enumeration can be exponentially more redundant than the causal output, and symbolic duplicate removal is the nonroutine bridge from a structural class to usable possible-effect analysis.
body.gap: WienobstBannachLiskiewicz2023 counts ordinary Markov-equivalent DAGs by clique-picking, and GuoPerkovic2022EfficientLS estimates effects for enumerated parent sets; neither quotients a transported-partition component by equality of rational effect maps.
body.consumer: Large sparse components could feed IDA-style effect analysis without storing every observationally equivalent blocked state.

obligation.what_is_open: Whether exact quotienting by equality of the rational maps \(g_E\) admits deterministic output-polynomial total time or polynomial delay while retaining a certificate for every state.
obligation.obstruction: Compact arithmetic-circuit equality for the rational effect maps reduces after denominator clearing to exact polynomial identity testing; deterministic polynomial-time canonicalization is not supplied by the frozen core. In addition, the number of states can be much larger than the number of distinct functionals, so ordinary breadth-first traversal does not give delay measured in distinct outputs.
obligation.attempted: The component was enumerated by legal-reversal breadth-first search, transported partitions were reconstructed from endpoint parent sets and invariant nonsingleton families, and exact rational functions were compared after clearing denominators. This closes correctness and path independence but not the requested complexity bound.
obligation.partial_result: There is a terminating exact procedure, but no output-polynomial or polynomial-delay bound is established. Breadth-first search enumerates every state in \(\mathcal R(C)\), stores the shortest predecessor certificate of length \(\delta(C,E)\), and computes each \(g_E\) as a rational arithmetic expression. The transported partition is path independent because the endpoint graph and the invariant families \((\mathcal N_j)_{j\in V}\) uniquely determine it. Equality of two resulting rational maps is decidable by cross-multiplying their positive Gram-determinant denominators and expanding the resulting polynomial identity, so exact equality classes and one representative per class can be returned after all states are visited. This proves finite exact duplicate removal with shortest certificates, but its running time is controlled by \(|\mathcal R(C)|\) and by expanded polynomial size, not by the number of distinct effect functionals.
